column6: rationale -- scripts/gen-membudget.py; docs/SIZING.md "Memory budgets"; CONTRIBUTING.md "Memory budgets" for flipping an open row.

an aggregate scan that can spill: its group table (held to hash memory at the end of each unit; a process of a scan with workers holds at most group_par_factor (2) times hash memory, past which the statement runs again as PostgreSQL plans it), the results of the finished table, the caches of the values of its expressions (4 MB at most), the table of an IN list (half of hash memory at most), the state of the partitions of the scan (8 kB each, 2,048 at the default work_mem) and one superblock of write buffer rows (6 MB for 1 kB rows); the rows a scan reads again from the heap hold one whole document as SQL does, which is the size of the document, not of the table (shred_elems)

the groups of an aggregate scan that cannot spill (a top-N or an order on a key that is not an integer, a date or a timestamp, ordered-set aggregates, grouping sets, a two level aggregate, an ungrouped aggregate): the table grows to the bound of the planner, group_nospill_factor (32) times the larger of hash memory and 8 MB, and ends the scan past it (3.5 MB for 5 groups of a percentile)
the table of a lookup join, hashed by key: 22.8 MB measured, it follows the rows of the dimension table (slope row lookup_join_label)
the inverted buffer of a CREATE INDEX of a search index, its runs and the page of text (9.5 MB held at maintenance_work_mem 1MB: 13.6 MB)
the runs and the inverted buffer of a merge of search segments
the sort of the documents of a sealed segment

the state of a search scan: each open segment holds about 165 kB (a 64 kB dictionary block, its header and stream reader), up to 128 segments (24 MB), plus 8 MB of cursors, candidates and top-N; 0.5 MB at 2 segments, 9.8 MB at 60
the walk of one segment and the heap check of sift.verify: a context for each segment, deleted at its end (before: 115 MB held for 60 segments, now 0.2 MB)

the choice between reading the heap through a btree on the key and the key ranges of a CREATE INDEX of a sift_col index with key_cut: the walk of the leaf level of a btree through a simulated cache of the heap blocks (at most 65,536 blocks of 24 bytes and their hash entries, 5 MB, whatever shared_buffers is: the cache is scaled down by a power of two to it), the 512 keys the ranges of a parallel build are cut at, and the rows of superblocks spread over the table that price the key ranges' files (at most 16,384 rows or 8 MB)

the rows, runs and segment writer of CREATE INDEX of a sift_col index: twice the budget of its runs (col_build_budget: half of maintenance_work_mem, never under the serial floor of 64 MB, SIFT_COL_BUILD_SERIAL_BUDGET) plus 16 MB for the superblock in hand and the writer's fixed parts. Exact bytes (col_build_exact_memory, 8-page flavour, the floors lowered with sift.test_limits so that maintenance_work_mem cuts the runs): a key_cut build holds 2.1 times its run budget and the files of the at most 512 ranges of its runs (8.3 kB each): 10.1 MB at 8 MB and 18.5 MB at 16 MB with a fitted per-row term of 5 and -4 bytes over 40,000 to 120,000 rows, 4.8 to 6.0 MB at 1 MB, 6.6 to 8.1 MB under a serial floor of 2 MB (19 bytes a row); a build without key_cut holds 1.35 times its writer budget, (maintenance_work_mem - 30 MB) / 1.4: 6 MB at 36 MB, 9.4 MB at 40 MB. Under the shipped floor the memory grows with the rows only until the first run fills the floor, 155 bytes a row of the rows held and 0.6 of them more in the writer of the run (dictionaries of unique strings, point directories): 52.6, 79.8, 86.9 and 75.7 MB at 200,000, 400,000, 800,000 and 1,600,000 rows of 8 columns at any maintenance_work_mem up to 128 MB, the same on 5.0.2, and flat from there (the rows past the first run go to the key ranges' files, chunks held to the floor); the rows of the first run and the chunks made from them are no longer held together

the choice of the path of a CREATE INDEX or REINDEX of a sift_col index (col/build/choose.c): the directory of the index a REINDEX replaces and the copies of its segments and write buffers (56 bytes an entry, at most the 32,768 of a directory: 3.5 MB; 14 kB at 128 entries), the texts of the NOTICE; it does not follow the rows of the table or of the index

the open units of a CREATE INDEX of a sift_col index with key_cut, while the table is scanned: the rows of each value of the key that fills units, packed as the spool packs them, and the units that are complete and wait for their segment: a quarter and a half of the memory the plan gave the open path (the budget less what the files of the key ranges keep: a quarter of it and as much more as the share of the rows the open units take), one unit over (col/build/open.c); the cut of a unit and the segment writer are contexts of their own

the chunks of the temporary files of the key ranges of a CREATE INDEX of a sift_col index with key_cut, while the table is scanned: for each range that has rows a batch of up to a chunk of rows and the dictionaries of its strings, which a plan made from the first run holds to the build budget between all the ranges (a range writes its chunk when it holds that many rows or its share of the memory); the rows of a build whose budget does not hold a chunk of a few hundred rows for each range are packed in blocks and hold 32 kB for each

the walk over the journal records of the tombstone log of an index (the changed keys of a scope or a connected parent): one block of a run and the blocks of its context, whatever the number of records; the table of the distinct keys, which the read refuses past its cap, is the result's and is not in the scope

the dead addresses one statement holds before it writes them to the tombstone log of an index (col/track_dv.c): at most a million, 8 bytes each, the same again sorted for the lookup, the deletion records made from them (at most a slot of 32 bytes for each address) and the open units of one segment at a time, whatever the number of rows the statement deletes (the statement writes and goes on past a million); exact bytes (test/sql/col_dv_memory.sql, a quarter of the rows deleted): 114,208 at 3,000 rows deleted, 181,776 at 6,000, 271,312 at 9,000 and 306,064 at 12,000: 21 bytes a deleted row

the rows that the deletion records of the tombstone log end in the units a scan reads (col/scan/dvec.c): one bit for each row of a unit that holds a deleted row (a unit with none keeps nothing), the table of the units asked about and one scratch unit; a million rows deleted scattered over every unit of a scan hold 1/8 byte for each row of the index, so the scan of a very large index needs more than the constant until the overlay of a unit is dropped when the scan leaves it; exact bytes (a quarter of the rows deleted, units of about 10,000 rows): 25,776 at 2 units and 33,968 at 3, 4 and 5 (the 8 kB blocks of the allocator: 0.23 B a row of the table between 12,000 and 48,000 rows), made of the record in hand and one unit of scratch (about 8 kB) and, for each unit that has a record, a table entry of 40 bytes and its rows at 1 bit each

the fold, the carry to marks and the drop of the deletion records (col/maint/dvfold.c): the directory in hand, one open segment at a time (its headers and unit directory) and four unit-sized arrays (rows, live bits, record bits, the record in hand); exact bytes: 341,392 at every size from 12,000 to 48,000 rows

the keys of the marks the fold of the tombstone log clears (sift.tomb_log_limit as many keys as the log may keep bytes, 8 bytes each) and the temp file the keys past them wait in: a chunk of the keys at a time, whatever the number of marks

the rows of the write buffers of the index a REINDEX replaces, decoded into batches and written as runs before the merge by the key takes them with the old segments: they follow the bytes of the buffers (write_buffer_limit of each, at most the buffers of the directory), not the rows of the index (523,296 / 1,958,344 / 4,740,456 bytes for 2,000 / 8,000 / 30,000 buffered rows); the merge itself is the scope col_merge

the cells of one leaf of the decision of the automatic key_cut: the rows of the sampled superblocks as one cell each in a buffer, sorted (the rows of one superblock at least, 74,496 at the most, 1.2 MB with the sort's copy; as many as half of what maintenance_work_mem has left takes otherwise): a buffer that holds them all is read as it is, a smaller one is written as runs of cells (the rows of a value in a superblock counted) that a tournament tree merges in the order of the values, a cursor for each of at most 256 runs (16 kB each when the run is on the temporary file); the runs are kept in memory while the bytes of the sample's spools stay under maintenance_work_mem and on a temporary file past it

the sample of the automatic key_cut of CREATE INDEX, REINDEX and sift.key_cut_decision: its rows (8 bytes of address and 8 for each of at most 8 leaves, 80 bytes at the most) in a spool kept in memory up to maintenance_work_mem and on a temporary file past it, the zones of the leaves and the state of the index; the rows are written to the spool as the heap gives them, and the decision does not hold more rows, whatever the table has

the model of the size of an index cut by a key or by the superblock: the keys of the rows of the sampled superblocks sorted a buffer at a time (the rows of one superblock at least, 6 MB with the sort) into runs of a spool, merged in the order of the key (a sample that is in memory is read where it is, a sample on the temporary file goes with a copy of each row), the window of the merge a unit of the cut and the rows the cut looks ahead (149,000 rows of 104 bytes at the most, 27 MB), the columns of the unit being measured (up to 26 MB) and 8 bytes for each leaf and 2 for each unit of the cut (4.5 MB at the most)

the input segments, one unit of rows of each, and the partition being written by a column merge: 12 to 14 MB at the default maintenance_work_mem on small tables, 36 to 47 MB on 1,600,000 rows at 1 and 4 MB (col_merge_exact_memory pins the exact bytes); col_merge_window holds the decoded units of the inputs to a budget. What is open is the share of the participants: each participant of a merge cut in slices takes the whole of maintenance_work_mem for its writer (sift_colw_budget) and a quarter of it for its window (merge_window.c), where PostgreSQL's parallel builds give each a share, so a merge of N participants may hold N times the budget; and the contexts of the inputs of a merge that one process makes of 15 inputs hold 26 to 35 MB at 40,000 to 60,000 rows at 8 MB of maintenance_work_mem (1.7 to 2.3 MB for each, in the context of the merge, not in the window) in 2 of 8 parallel builds of a key_cut index on the 8-page flavour, whichever process ends the merge; the intended budget is maintenance_work_mem plus a constant

the state of the inputs of a column merge that follows no budget: each input's open segment (its header, unit directory and zones: 8 kB to 100 kB) and, for the inputs open at the key the merge is at, the parsed dictionary of each of its string leaves (2.2 bytes for each byte of the input: 22 bytes a row of a unique text leaf). A key_cut merge opens an input, decodes its first unit and parses its dictionaries when its rows reach the lowest key of that input (read from the zones of the unit, col/order.c wake_inputs) and gives them back at its last unit: at most 3 times the bytes of the inputs that hold the key in hand plus 32 kB for each input (col_merge_flat_memory asserts it in exact bytes at 12,000 to 168,000 rows: inputs that hold a key range each are open one at a time, 341 kB of dictionaries at 168,000 rows against 4.4 MB when every input is opened at the first row, and the same segments; inputs that all hold the whole range are open together, 3.9 MB). The inputs of a merge are partitions of the bytes maintenance_work_mem sizes (maint_part_kb_for) and the overlays that follow them, but any number of overlays overlaps the key in hand, so the bound is the overlap and not maintenance_work_mem; the intended budget is maintenance_work_mem plus a constant, which needs the inputs that overlap to be read without parsing their dictionary (a lookup in the stream where the stored form allows it: forms 0, 2, 3 and 5, not the compact form 1, which is read whole): open

the decoded units of the inputs of a column merge and the batch they are folded into (col/maint/merge_window.c): the units of a step are folded at a quarter of maintenance_work_mem (4 MB at least), so a merge holds the units of a step, the one they are folded into and the empty batches it lends again, whatever the number of its inputs: 8.9 MB at 1 MB of maintenance_work_mem for 13 inputs of 74,496-row units, the same at 50,000 to 200,000 rows (col_merge_flat_memory: 1.0 to 2.2 MB at 8-page units from 12,000 to 168,000 rows)
the decoded unit of the sweep of overflow records (4.7 MB)
the view of the segments the rewrite rule judges (1 kB)

the answers a scope fill remembers of its btree probes (a member and its keys): forgotten at the next batch once they pass a quarter of maintenance_work_mem, and a batch holds its own (3 pairs a row of 200,000 rows, kept to 262,144 entries: 8 MB of entries, 10 MB of keys; kept to the quarter: 0.5 MB at 1 MB)

the units decoded and the sorted runs of a scope refill. Exact bytes at 4 MB of maintenance_work_mem with the floors lowered to 1 MB (6.1, 7.1, 7.4, 8.1, 9.5 and 11.2 MB at 10,000, 20,000, 40,000, 80,000, 160,000 and 320,000 rows, 3 entries a row): the sort holds 2.08 to 2.16 MB at every size (half of maintenance_work_mem and 4%, bounded); the list of pairs the fill keeps is held to maintenance_work_mem / 8 for each scope (the context of the refill: 0.3 MB at 10,000 rows, 1.5 MB at 320,000); the writer of the scope segments is cut when its own estimate passes its budget, and holds 3.7 times that at 44,000 rows (84 bytes a row for an estimate of 22) and 5.6 times at 49,000 rows of a table of 320,000 (118 bytes a row), where its units are larger: 3.7 to 5.8 MB at a budget of 1 MB. The sort is bounded; the row stays open on the writer, whose actual bytes are a multiple of its budget that grows with the rows of the table (at 320,000 rows the units of the dimension rows are larger); the intended budget is maintenance_work_mem plus a constant

the entries a backend caches of the tombstone log of an index, for a scan, VACUUM or the fold of the marks: kept to sift.tomb_log_limit, the rest in sorted runs on temp files; a writer and a read of the header (completeness, key journal) cache none (a scoped concurrent build of 200,000 rows cached 600,000 entries, 32 MB, to read a header)
the two sorts and the window of row hashes of sift.col_verify, each held to maintenance_work_mem (24 MB at the default, 17.6 MB at 4 MB)

the reader of the write buffer of a column index: it copies the records of the buffer to sort them by key, each at its size, and holds one entry of 40 bytes a row: 12.6 MB at the default buffer, 612 bytes a row in the crash test of the buffer (col_wbuf_crash: a 512 kB buffer whose open segment held 165,000 rows, 101 MB, on a host where its seal lagged behind eight appenders; 141 MB when the copies were one buffer that doubled), so the test stops its calls at 80,000 rows: 49 MB; the intended budget is work_mem plus a constant, which a buffer past its limit exceeds: open

the dictionaries of the text leaves of a segment writer and the rows counted for their codes (col/seg_write): held per segment and under the budget the segment is cut at (test col_writer_terms_mem), but a table that needs more segments than the directory holds raises the budget to its rows over the segments left, and the dictionary then follows the rows of a segment (57 bytes a row of unique 32-byte strings at 3 segments)

the blocks of the order arrays a segment writer builds when its last unit is in (col/spool.h, col/gorder.c): the entries still held, a reader block of 8 kB for each of the at most 64 runs a leaf merges, the directory and the string table of each block built

the arrays of the point directories and of the grouped order arrays of a segment writer and the tables built from them (col/seg_write): held per segment like the dictionaries, and in proportion to the rows of a segment (51 bytes a row at 3 segments) when the directory of segments is too small for the budget

the entries of the order arrays a segment writer holds until its last unit is in (col/spool.h): a buffer of SIFT_ESET_ROWS entries (256 kB) for each leaf and each of its two regions, the file buffers and the runs of the levels of a leaf that spilled, the blocks built and the merge in hand: the writer weighs the arrays as they would be in memory (16 bytes an entry), a segment is cut at that weight, so what it holds is under its budget
the directory snapshot and the steps of the ambulkdelete and amvacuumcleanup of an index, with the promotions and merges the cleanup runs inside it (8.6 MB at the default maintenance_work_mem)
what one step of the maintenance worker holds besides its promotion or merge, once they end (0.16 MB measured)

the batch of entries a backend reads from the pages of a tombstone log before it sorts them into the log it keeps (sift_table and sift_col): a chunk of a quarter of the entries the limit lets the log keep, and one page; whatever the length of the log
the segment read of a value store usage count, reset at each segment (88 kB)
